confirmed.title: On a page with a shown original (video, map, iframe), a popup the page appends to <body> and focuses during a Sift click still closes at once (F1102 on portal pages)
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:3432 (clickSwallowed(el, () => proxy.click(el))); src/content/shield.ts:51-62 (ancestors of a portal stay out of inert); src/content/index.ts:2598 (new <body> children become inert only in the observer callback, after the click)
confirmed.evidence: Fixture /fx/r12int-focusportal.html is r11int-focusclose.html plus one iframe, so Sift shows a portal and <body> is not inert as a whole. In Sift, Invite people logs ['share open','share closed'] and no sheet stays open. On the original it logs ['share open'] with focus on #copyurl. A focus-event trace in Sift shows the sequence. blur on Sift's button (rel=copyurl), then focusin on #copyurl: the page's focus() succeeded because the new popup was not inert. Then 'inert sharebox=true' (refreshShield), then blur and focusout on #copyurl (rel=null), then the page removes the popup 150 ms later. Account and Rename work on this fixture: their elements sit in subtrees that were already inert.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 ./scripts/chrome.sh start; cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r12int; FX=http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r12int-focusportal.html SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun focusclose.ts sift 'Invite people' prints log ['share open','share closed']. The same with 'orig' prints ['share open'] and docActive button#copyurl.
confirmed.suspectedCause: With any portal, desired() keeps <body> and the portal's ancestors out of inert. A node the page appends to one of them during the replayed click is reachable until the MutationObserver's refreshShield runs. So the page's focus() lands for real, out of Sift. Making the node inert afterwards blurs it, and widgets that close on blur or focusout close (React portals, menus and share popups that focus their first item). Lead: around proxy.click in H.act, tell the page-world helper that a Sift click is running (a sift-click start/end event). While it runs, the helper's focus wrapper skips the native focus() for targets outside [data-sift-portal] and fires sift-focus, as it does for inert targets. Refreshing the shield sooner does not help, because it still blurs.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed. I would rate it medium to high: the popup fails completely, but only on pages that have both a shown portal and a popup that closes on blur. On /fx/r12int-focusportal.html, focusclose.ts with 'Invite people' logged ['share open','share closed'] in Sift in 3 runs (1.5 s, 1.5 s and 4 s waits). No sheet opened and Sift's focus went back to its 'Invite people' button. With Sift off, 2 runs logged ['share open'] with document.activeElement = button#copyurl. On /fx/r11int-focusclose.html (the same page without the iframe), Sift logged ['share open'] twice, with the sheet shown and focus on 'Copy invite link'. So the shown portal is what breaks it. Before the click, my own trace showed body.inert=false, one [data-sift-portal], and data-sift-inert only on header, h1, p, the 4 sections and p#log. During the click, the events ran in this order: blur on Sift's button (rel=#copyurl), then focus and focusin on button#copyurl. So the page's focus() really landed, because #sharebox was a new, non-inert child of <body>. Next came 'added sharebox inert=true' (the observer's refreshShield), then blur and focusout on #copyurl (rel=null). The page then removed the box. Account and Rename still work on this page (['menu open'] and ['editing'] with focus in Sift's textarea), as the reporter said. The mechanism matches the code. In desired() (src/content/shield.ts), once there are exceptions, <body> and the portal's ancestors stay out of inert. New body children are made inert only in the MutationObserver callback (src/content/index.ts ~2598). That callback cannot run during the synchronous proxy.click inside clickSwallowed (index.ts ~3432).
confirmed.fix: Mark the Sift click in the page-world helper, the same way sift-enter and sift-leave with detail 'key' are handled in src/main/index.ts. In H.act (src/content/index.ts ~3432), dispatch a start event before clickSwallowed(el, () => proxy.click(el)) and an end event in a finally. In the focus wrapper in src/main/index.ts (~194, the one that dispatches sift-focus), while that flag is set, skip the native focus() for a target that is not inside [data-sift-portal] and dispatch sift-focus. Sift's existing follow logic (followPageFocus) then moves focus to its copy, as it already does when <body> is inert. Calling refreshShield earlier does not help, because it still blurs the popup.

On /fx/r10skep-ariadate.html: KEYS=ArrowRight leaves the page month at 'mm/Empty' but Sift's month box reads 'Empty'. KEYS=Backspace gives the same in the month box. KEYS=1,2,ArrowLeft leaves Sift's day box at 'Empty' while the page shows 'dd'. 1,2,2,5 then 3 Backspaces leaves Sift's year box at 'Empty'. rejected.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 ./scripts/chrome.sh start; cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r12int; KEYS=ArrowRight SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun aria.ts sift prints 'page: mm/Empty | … | sift: Empty/Empty | dd/Empty | yyyy/Empty'.
rejected.suspectedCause: Round 11 changed the render (f.shown) but not keyAct's optimistic text update. In keyAct, draw the page element's own text, (el.textContent ?? '').trim(), as the visible text, and keep aria-valuetext only as the attribute.
rejected.verdict: It reproduces, but I rate it polish, not medium. With aria.ts and my own script on /fx/r10skep-ariadate.html, the boxes show mm, dd and yyyy on load. After ArrowRight, Sift's month box reads 'Empty' while the page shows 'mm' (read after 1.5 s and after 4 s). After Backspace, I saw the same twice. After 1,2,ArrowLeft, the day box reads 'Empty' while the page shows 'dd'. After 1,2,ArrowLeft,ArrowRight, the month box reads '12 – December' while the page shows '12'. The cause is as described. keyAct (src/content/index.ts ~1013-1021) writes aria-valuetext into the box's text node. The next render's f.shown is unchanged ('mm'), so Preact leaves the text node alone. But the text is always the page's own accurate value text for that same segment, never a wrong value. Each box now has a visible label ('month, Reservation date', 'day, Reservation date', 'year, Reservation date', seen in my screenshot). The screen-reader value is correct, and the field stays fully usable. So the only harm is wording ('Empty' in place of the 'mm' hint). This is also not a regression: before round 11 the boxes always showed aria-valuetext. For whoever wants it anyway, the one-line fix is in keyAct: draw (el.textContent ?? '').trim() as the visible text and keep aria-valuetext only as the attribute.

stillOpen.evidence: weather.com today (/weather/today/l/37.7749,-122.4194), original [data-testid=TemperatureValue] vs Sift '\d+°', timed with fp2t.ts. Unthrottled at load 8-11, they were equal in 5 of 5 runs: 7458/7458, 5226/5226, 4348/4348, 5063/5063 and 9016/9016 ms. At 4x CPU throttle they were equal in 13 of 14 runs, for example 27229/27229, 16113/16113, 14261/14261 and 13008/13008. Once, at load 16.5, Sift was 2.2 s later: 41775/43980 ms. The merged diff does not touch schedule() or contentShown(). Sift's first content comes far earlier than the original's (median 1367 vs 7942 ms). Under heavy CPU pressure, the forecast still sometimes arrives seconds after the page shows it. This is rarer than round 10's 2 of 23.

skeptic.verdict: Partly fixed holds. The lag is still there, and in my runs it was not rarer than in round 10. I used the claimant's fp2t.ts against sift-test-3 (port 9463, tab skeptic) on weather.com today, comparing the original [data-testid=TemperatureValue] with Sift's main matching '\d+°'. Unthrottled (load 7-8), they were equal 4 of 4 times: 5888, 4190, 3616 and 3139 ms. At 4x throttle I ran three sets. First set (load 4-8): equal 8 of 8. Second set (load 6-8): Sift was later 2 of 10 times, 12188/14795 and 14221/17547. Third set (load 8-10.5): Sift was later 3 of 10 times, 18682/29830, 22566/28510 and 13452/16805. So at 4x Sift was later 5 of 28 times, not the claimed 1 of 14. At 6x (load 2-7), it was later 1 of 26 times: 16557/22679. The trace shows a real gap. In one snapshot, the original already had the temperature while Sift showed only the page frame. That frame was 105 characters: 'San Francisco Weather ... Today's Outlook ... Daily Forecast Next 10 Days'. In other runs the frame came with the 'Trending Now' video list, 391 characters. The size of each lag is uncertain. Under throttle, a single poll took 2 to 11 s, so the 11 s figure is mostly poll latency. The direction of the gap is still clear. A mutation probe shows the temperature arrives as added elements, not as a text-only change. So the 2500 ms 'minor' floor is not the cause. The round 11 merge did not touch schedule(), contentShown(), stillLoading() or thinView(). I checked git diff 0b07e6b..7bd95ba, and src matches HEAD. Severity is medium only on slow or busy machines. Unthrottled it is fine.
skeptic.fix: In src/content/index.ts there are two causes. First, thinView() treats the frame plus the 'Trending Now' video list as real content because it is over 200 characters. Once that happens, contentShown() is true and the forecast goes through the routine path. That path waits lastDur*3, then an idle callback with a 600 ms timeout. Fix: keep the page counted as loading until a non-minor batch of 400 or more characters has been read since the frame. Or, in schedule(), skip requestIdleCallback and cap d at about 300 ms while stillLoading() and readyState is complete. Second, on the loading path, runs are spaced by lastDur*3. With slow extractions at 4x, that alone is several seconds. While stillLoading(), cap that spacing at about 1x lastDur for a run triggered by grew.
